description: The bar chart illustrates the average number of likes received by posts grouped by their similarity scores, as analyzed in the paper “How to Generate Popular Post Headlines on Social Media.” The horizontal axis categorizes posts into five bins based on the similarity range of their most similar group: (0,90], (90,180], (180,270], (270,360], and (360,450]. The vertical axis, labeled “Avg. Like #,” measures the average number of likes on a linear scale ranging from 400 to 600, with tick marks at intervals of 50. Each bar is light blue and topped with vertical error bars indicating variability. The first bar, corresponding to the (0,90] similarity range, reaches approximately 600 likes — the highest among all groups. The second bar, (90,180], is slightly lower at around 565 likes. The third bar, (180,270], is approximately 570 likes. The fourth bar, (270,360], rises again to about 595 likes, and the fifth bar, (360,450], settles at roughly 585 likes. The chart suggests that posts with very low similarity (0–90) and moderate-to-high similarity (270–360) tend to receive the highest average engagement, while those in the mid-range (90–180) receive the least. No bars are shaded or emphasized differently; all are uniformly styled.
